title: ADNOC Signs 10-Year LNG Supply Deal With India's Gujarat Energy, From 2028
excerpt: The agreement covers up to 4 million tonnes of LNG over a decade, is ADNOC's fifth LNG supply deal in India, and marks the first sale from XRG's international portfolio.
body:
• ADNOC has signed a 10-year liquefied natural gas sale and purchase agreement with India's Gujarat Energy, the Abu Dhabi company said on Friday.
  • Gujarat Energy will receive up to 4 million tonnes of LNG in total over the decade, with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2028 — an average of up to 400,000 tonnes a year if spread evenly.
  • It is ADNOC's fifth LNG supply agreement in India and the first sale from the international portfolio of its investment arm, XRG.
  • Financial terms were not disclosed; Gujarat Energy operates city gas distribution across 44 districts in six Indian states.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company has signed a 10-year liquefied natural gas supply agreement with India's Gujarat Energy, expanding its presence in one of Asia's key LNG markets, Reuters reported on Friday.

Under the agreement, Gujarat Energy will receive up to 4 million tonnes of LNG over ten years, with shipments due to begin in 2028, according to the company statement reported by OilPrice.com and the Economic Times. The statement set a cap on total volumes, the term and the start date, but did not provide an annual delivery schedule or the contract's financial value.

First sale from XRG's international portfolio

The gas will be sourced from the international portfolio of XRG, ADNOC's international investment company — making this the first sale of molecules from that portfolio. It is ADNOC's fifth LNG supply agreement in India, following deals that include a January agreement by ADNOC Gas to supply 500,000 tonnes annually to Hindustan Petroleum for ten years.

The deal feeds ADNOC's global LNG marketing and trading platform, launched in the Abu Dhabi Global Market in July 2026. The platform has now signed supply agreements with INPEX in Japan, Gulf Group in Thailand and Gujarat Energy in India, and is targeting 47 million tonnes per annum of marketable LNG beyond 2030 as ADNOC seeks a place among the world's leading LNG suppliers.

"This agreement with Gujarat Energy strengthens ADNOC's long-standing energy partnership with customers in India."

— Rashid Al Mazrouei, Chief Marketing and Origination Officer (LNG), ADNOC

The buyer

Gujarat Energy, formerly Gujarat Gas, adopted its new name in May 2026 after a restructuring that combined Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation, Gujarat State Petronet and GSPC Energy. The state-owned company runs a city gas distribution network covering 44 districts across six Indian states, supplying industrial, commercial and residential customers, and also operates in gas trading and exploration. For Gujarat Energy, the agreement adds a long-dated, portfolio-sourced supply line to its procurement book from 2028.

What to watch

The contract's start is still more than a year away, and ADNOC has not disclosed pricing or delivery points. India's petroleum ministry has said the UAE supplies roughly 15 to 20 per cent of India's total energy imports — the backdrop against which this fifth Indian LNG agreement lands. The next facts to watch are the delivery schedule, once published, and whether the XRG platform adds further Asian buyers toward its 47 mtpa target.
